article.articleHeadline: Mandaue intensifies dengue prevention after 2 deaths in November
article.articleSummary: Two dengue-related deaths in November in Mandaue City prompted surveillance by the City Health Office. The fatalities were residents of Barangay Tabok and Barangay Umapad. Officials say dengue cases are rising this year versus 2025 (520 cases, 3 deaths); 2026 tally is not disclosed, with Jan–July reports indicating 373 cases and 1 death. The CHO automatically dispatches surveillance teams for any dengue infection or fatality, conducts household checks to map symptom duration, delays in seeking care, and identify mosquito breeding sites, and educates communities on prevention. Eliminating breeding sites remains the top measure. Residents are urged to follow DOH's 4S: search/destroy breeding sites, seek early consultation, practice self-protection, and support targeted spraying during outbreaks. Free lab tests (CBC, platelet count, NS1), paracetamol, and hydration are offered at dengue fast lanes. 27 barangays have activated dengue brigades; prevention is year-round, with emphasis during the rainy season, and regional cooperation is encouraged.

article.articleHeadline: Philippines vaccinates nearly 500,000 pigs against ASF as it races to rebuild hog sector
article.articleSummary: ASF in the Philippines: Nearly 500,000 pigs vaccinated under the DA's program, with 499,008 of 500,000 doses used (99.8%), across 54 farms in seven provinces and one government farm. Tarlac led with 287,620; Batangas 92,021; Bulacan 88,107; other provinces include Rizal, Laguna, Quezon and Pampanga. As of 22 October, active ASF infections persisted in 236 barangays across 23 provinces, while about 65% of previously affected areas have recovered; 716 cities/municipalities reclassified as buffer or surveillance zones, covering 64.68% of affected areas. Since ASF reached the Philippines in 2019, the outbreak devastated the hog sector; the government aims to repopulate and restore production to pre-ASF levels. A commercially approved vaccine (AVAC Live Vaccine from Vietnam) was approved in September; biosecurity programs (CABI) extend to 14 barangays and 258 backyard farmers; indemnification payments totaling PHP 49.8 million distributed across eight regions.

article.articleHeadline: Philippine Farmed Crustacean Vibrio Bacteria Show High Rifampicin and
article.articleSummary: Baseline surveillance across fourteen crustacean farms in ten Philippine provinces (Pangasinan, Zambales, Nueva Ecija, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, South Cotabato, Sarangani, Aklan, Capiz, Iloilo) analyzed 60 Vibrio isolates from whiteleg shrimp (Penaeus vannamei), black tiger shrimp (Penaeus monodon), giant freshwater prawns (Macrobrachium rosenbergii), and mangrove crabs (Scylla serrata). From 120 specimens collected April–October 2024, PCR-confirmed Vibrio species comprised V. harveyi (25%), V. alginolyticus (18.3%), V. vulnificus (16.7%), V. parahaemolyticus (15%), and 15% unclassified to species. Rifampicin resistance was observed in 81.7% of isolates, ampicillin in 45%; tetracycline 5%, chloramphenicol 3.3%, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1.7%. Ciprofloxacin resistance was absent; 21.7% showed intermediate susceptibility. Single-drug resistance dominated (45%), with 40% rifampicin resistance alone; dual ampicillin–rifampicin in 36.7%. True multidrug resistance (three classes) occurred in three postlarval isolates (MARI 0.50). PCR screening of 13 resistance determinants showed limited concordance with phenotypic resistance.

article.articleHeadline: Study Analyzes Adaptive Rollout of Molecular Tuberculosis Tests Across the
article.articleSummary: Philippines' rollout of World Health Organization-recommended rapid diagnostic tests for tuberculosis (mWRDs) faced delays risking missed drug-resistant TB diagnoses. A national case study—twelve interviews with policy actors and twenty policy texts—analyzed with Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and mapped to Greenhalgh's NASSS framework. Peer-learning led policymakers to abandon replacing microscopes with mWRDs in favor of a smaller set of machines connected by dedicated specimen transport riders. This enabled sputum collection at primary care facilities and created a dynamic diagnostic network balancing lab efficiency, machine use, and geographic equity. mWRD platforms evolved into multi-disease infrastructure aligned with universal health coverage and a life-stage health system approach. Donor–national alignment and pilot initiatives spurred innovations. The study frames diagnostic scale-up as adaptive, iterative, guiding deployment of next-generation near-patient molecular tests amid funding constraints in the Philippines.

The institute promotes direct engagement with its experts and highlights ongoing CDC Foundation support since 2017. The push for knowledge translation involves researchers, policymakers, and media to ensure findings reach the public and inform responses to outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Contained Ebola With Preparation, Not Luck. Africa Needs More of the Same
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on 11 November 2026, 37 days after recording the country’s first Ebola case, with zero community transmission to date; if no new cases emerge in the next six weeks, Kenya will be declared Ebola-free on 23 December 2026. The rapid containment was driven by proactive preparation: in June, Kenya’s KNPHI invited a Ugandan epidemiologist to train about 200 Kenyan health workers on outbreak investigation and alert response, with virtual networks enabling rapid nationwide communication. Virtual networks—supported by Project ECHO—are highlighted as critical for expanding local capacity, incorporating community voices, and respecting local burial practices. Senegal, Zambia, and Sudan are cited as successful examples of using digital learning to reach frontline workers and adapt guidance in real time. The piece argues for sustained investment in such networks, amid funding cuts to WHO and global health programs, to prepare for future crises.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、運ではなく備えでエボラを封じ込めた。アフリカにはさらなる同様の取り組みが必要
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はケニアにおけるエボラ流行がすでに封じ込められ、地域内感染ゼロで終息に向かっている成功事例の振り返り・政策提言記事であり、対象国における新規の感染症シグナルではない。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアでのエボラ封じ込め成功事例であり、ケニアは対象国リストに含まれない。ザンビア・セネガル・スーダンはデジタル学習ネットワーク活用の成功例として言及されているのみで、これらの国で実際にエボラ流行が発生しているとの記述はないため verified_locations には含めない。
